concepts.name: More features of the Government of India Act 1935

questions.q: Which one of the following was NOT provided for by the Government of India Act of 1935?
questions.a: Continuation of the Council of India set up in 1858
o: Continuation of the Council of India set up in 1858
A Federal Court, which was set up in 1937
A Reserve Bank of India to control currency and credit
An Auditor-General of India to audit federal and provincial accounts
questions.e: p.33: the 1935 Act abolished the Council of India established by the Act of 1858. The Federal Court, the Reserve Bank and the Auditor-General were all provided for (pp.33-34).
w: p.34: the Federal Court was provided for and set up in 1937.
p.33: the Reserve Bank of India was provided for by the 1935 Act.
p.34: the Auditor-General was provided for in the 1935 Act.

questions.q: The Federal Court, provided for by the Government of India Act of 1935, was set up in the year
questions.e: p.34: the Federal Court was set up in 1937.
w: The Act is of 1935, but the Court was set up later.
1939 is the year provincial autonomy was discontinued (p.33), not the Court's year.
1947 is the year of independence.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of provinces was created by the Government of India Act of 1935?
questions.e: p.34: the Act created two new provinces of Orissa and Sind.
w: Punjab already had a legislative council from 1897 (p.30), so it was not new; only Orissa is new here.
Madras was one of the presidencies from 1773 (p.25), so it was not new; only Sind is new here.
Burma was separated from India, not made a province (p.34).

questions.q: The Auditor-General of India, provided for by the Government of India Act of 1935, was to audit the accounts of
o: the federation and the princely states
questions.e: p.34: the Auditor-General was to audit the accounts of the federation and the provinces.
w: p.34: it covered the provinces as well as the federation.
p.34: it covered the federation as well as the provinces.
p.34: the audit covered the federation and the provinces; the princely states are not named.

questions.q: Under the Government of India Act of 1935 the proportion of the total population that got the right to vote was about
questions.e: p.33: the franchise was extended and about 14 per cent of the total population got the voting right.
w: Digit reversal; the text gives 14.
Too low; the text gives 14.
Far too high; the text gives 14.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Government of India Act of 1935:

1. The Act retained the Council of India established by the Government of India Act of 1858 as an advisory body.
2. About 14 per cent of the total population got the right to vote under the 1935 Act.
3. The All-India Federation envisaged by the Act never came into being because the princely states did not join it.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: p.33: that Council was abolished and the Secretary of State was given a team of advisors. Statement 2 is correct: p.33: the Act extended the franchise and about 14 per cent of the total population got the voting right. Statement 3 is correct: p.33: the princely states did not join.
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.33
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.33
'3 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.33

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Government of India Act of 1935:

1. The recommendations of the Simon Commission were incorporated in full in the Act of 1935.
2. The Act was a lengthy and detailed document having 231 Sections and 10 Schedules.
3. The Act divided powers into three lists: Federal (59 items), Provincial (54 items) and Concurrent (36 items).

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: p.32: it was the Joint Select Committee's recommendations that were incorporated, with certain changes. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.33: 321 Sections. Statement 3 is correct: p.33: 59, 54 and 36 items.
w: '2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.32
'1 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect: p.32
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.32

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Government of India Act of 1935:

1. Provincial autonomy took effect in 1937 and was discontinued in 1939.
2. The Act abolished dyarchy in the provinces and introduced provincial autonomy in its place.
3. The Act reserved a certain number of general seats for the depressed classes (Scheduled Castes).

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.33: in effect from 1937, discontinued in 1939. Statement 2 is correct: p.33: dyarchy abolished in the provinces; provincial autonomy introduced. Statement 3 is correct: p.33: reserved general seats for the depressed classes.
w: '1 and 2 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.33
'2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.33
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.33

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Government of India Act of 1935:

1. The Act separated Burma (now Myanmar) from India.
2. Residuary powers under the Act were given to the provinces.
3. The All-India Federation envisaged by the Act never came into being because the provinces did not join it.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.34: Burma was separated from India. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.33: they went to the Viceroy. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.33: it was the princely states that did not join.
w: '2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.34
'1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.34
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.34

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Government of India Act of 1935 and its background:

1. A Joint Public Service Commission was meant to serve two or more provinces.
2. The Federal Court provided for by the Act was set up in 1935 itself.
3. The Act introduced direct elections in the country for the first time.
4. The Simon Commission had seven members, all of them British.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.34: Joint Commission for two or more provinces. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.34: the Federal Court was set up in 1937. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.31: direct elections were introduced for the first time by the Act of 1919. Statement 4 is correct: p.32: seven members, all British.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.34
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.34
'2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.34

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Government of India Act of 1935:

1. The Act provided for safeguards to protect the interests of minorities.
2. The legislatures of eight of the eleven provinces were made bicameral.
3. Residuary powers under the Act were given to the Viceroy (Governor-General).

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.34: safeguards for minorities. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.33: six out of eleven provinces. Statement 3 is correct: p.33: residuary powers to the Viceroy.
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.34
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.34
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.34

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Government of India Act of 1935 and its background:

1. The Act extended special representation to labour (workers) as well as to women.
2. The Act provided for a Reserve Bank of India to control the currency and the budgets of the provinces.
3. The Communal Award of August 1932 was announced by the British Prime Minister, Stanley Baldwin.
4. A White Paper on Constitutional Reforms, prepared on the basis of the Round Table discussions, was submitted for the consideration of the Simon Commission.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.33: special representation to women and labour (workers). Statement 2 is incorrect: p.33: the Bank was for the currency and credit of the country, not provincial budgets. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.32: it was Ramsay MacDonald. Statement 4 is incorrect: p.32: the White Paper went to the Joint Select Committee of the British Parliament; the Simon Commission had reported in 1930.
w: '2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.33
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.33
'3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.33

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Government of India Act of 1935:

1. The Act was a lengthy and detailed document having 321 Sections and 10 Schedules.
2. The Act provided separate electorates for the depressed classes (Scheduled Castes) in the legislatures.
3. The legislatures of six of the eleven provinces were made bicameral.
4. The Act's provision for dyarchy at the Centre never came into operation.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.33: 321 Sections and 10 Schedules. Statement 2 is incorrect: pp.32-33: separate electorates for them were dropped; seats were reserved instead (Poona Pact). Statement 3 is correct: p.33: bicameralism in six out of eleven provinces. Statement 4 is correct: p.33: the provision did not come into operation at all.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.33
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.33
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.33

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Government of India Act of 1935:

1. The All-India Federation envisaged by the Act was to consist of the provinces, with the princely states left out of it.
2. The Act withdrew special representation from women and labour (workers).
3. The provisions of the Poona Pact were incorporated in the Government of India Act of 1935.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: p.33: the federation was to consist of provinces and princely states as units. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.33: it was extended to women and to labour. Statement 3 is correct: p.33: the Poona Pact's provisions were incorporated in the next Act, that of 1935.
w: '1 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.33
'2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.33
'1 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect: p.33

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Government of India Act of 1935:

1. The Act's provision for dyarchy at the Centre came into operation in 1937.
2. The British Government convened two Round Table conferences to consider the proposals of the Simon Commission.
3. The Act created two new provinces, Orissa and Sind.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: p.33: the Centre's dyarchy provision did not come into operation at all; provincial autonomy began in 1937. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.32: three conferences. Statement 3 is correct: p.34: the new provinces were Orissa and Sind. So exactly 1 correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 1 is correct (statements 3).
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 1 is correct (statements 3).
'All three' miscounts: exactly 1 is correct (statements 3).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Government of India Act of 1935:

1. The Simon Commission had seven members, including two Indians.
2. The Act divided powers into three lists: Federal (54 items), Provincial (59 items) and Concurrent (36 items).
3. The Act made no provision for safeguards to protect the interests of minorities.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: p.32: all the members were British, hence the boycott. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.33: the Federal List had 59 items and the Provincial 54. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.34: the Act provided for safeguards to protect the interests of minorities. So exactly 0 correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: none of the statements is correct.
'Only two' miscounts: none of the statements is correct.
'All three' miscounts: none of the statements is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Government of India Act of 1935:

1. The recommendations of the Joint Select Committee of the British Parliament were incorporated, with certain changes, in the Act of 1935.
2. The Act provided for a Federal Railway Authority to look after the administration of railways.
3. Provincial autonomy took effect in 1935 and was discontinued in 1937.
4. The British Government convened three Round Table conferences to consider the proposals of the Simon Commission.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.32: the Joint Select Committee's recommendations were incorporated with certain changes. Statement 2 is correct: p.34: the Federal Railway Authority was provided for. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.33: it took effect in 1937 and was discontinued in 1939. Statement 4 is correct: p.32: three round table conferences. So exactly 3 correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: exactly 3 are correct (statements 1, 2 and 4).
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 3 are correct (statements 1, 2 and 4).
'All four' miscounts: statement 3 is incorrect, so exactly 3 are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The composition of the central and provincial legislatures under the Government of India Act of 1935 was based on the modified Communal Award.
Statement-II: The provisions of the Poona Pact were incorporated in the Government of India Act of 1935.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: p.33: the composition of the central and provincial legislatures under the 1935 Act was based on the modified Communal Award. Statement-II is correct: p.33: 'Subsequently, the provisions of the Poona Pact were incorporated in the next Government of India Act of 1935'. The incorporation of the Pact (which modified the Award for the depressed classes) is what made the Act's composition rest on the modified Award, so II explains I.
w: Rejected: II is not a mere side fact: the Pact's incorporation (II) is the reason the composition rested on the modified Award (I): p.33.
Rejected: Statement-II is correct, as the Pact's provisions were incorporated in the 1935 Act: p.33.
Rejected: Statement-I is correct, as the composition was based on the modified Communal Award: p.33.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The Government of India Act of 1935 provided for a Joint Public Service Commission to serve the Centre and all the provinces together.
Statement-II: The Government of India Act of 1935 provided for a Provincial Public Service Commission and a Joint Public Service Commission for two or more provinces.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
o: Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
questions.e: Statement-I is incorrect: p.34: the Joint Commission was for two or more provinces, not for the Centre and all provinces. Statement-II is correct: p.34: Provincial and Joint Commissions were provided.
w: Rejected: I is incorrect (the Joint Commission was for two or more provinces, not the Centre), so II has nothing to explain: p.34.
Rejected: I is incorrect, so the two statements cannot both be correct: p.34.
Rejected: it is Statement-I that is incorrect and Statement-II that is correct, not the reverse: p.34.

questions.q:
Match the items in List-I with those in List-II.

List-I (Institution or office provided for in 1935)
A. Reserve Bank of India
B. Federal Court
C. Auditor-General of India
D. Federal Railway Authority

List-II (Description)
1. Audit of accounts of the federation and the provinces
2. Control of the currency and credit of the country
3. Set up in 1937
4. Administration of railways
questions.e: pp.33-34: the Bank controls currency and credit; the Court was set up in 1937; the Auditor-General audits federal and provincial accounts; the Authority looks after railways.
w: B and D are interchanged: Federal Court goes with 'Set up in 1937' and Federal Railway Authority goes with 'Administration of railways'.
A and B are interchanged: Reserve Bank of India goes with 'Control of the currency and credit of the country' and Federal Court goes with 'Set up in 1937'.
C and D are interchanged: Auditor-General of India goes with 'Audit of accounts of the federation and the provinces' and Federal Railway Authority goes with 'Administration of railways'.

concepts.name: Background to the Indian Independence Act 1947

questions.q: Attlee's announcement of 20 February 1947 was followed by agitation, demanding the partition of the country, by the
questions.e: p.34: the announcement was followed by agitation by the Muslim League demanding partition.
w: The Congress did not demand partition; it accepted the Mountbatten Plan (p.34).
The Chamber of Princes (Narendra Mandal) made no such demand.
The Assembly, formed in 1946, was framing a Constitution, not demanding partition.

questions.q: The boundaries between the Dominions of India and Pakistan at the time of partition were determined by a Boundary Commission under the chairmanship of
questions.e: p.38 (note 10): the Boundary Commission was headed by Radcliff (spelled so in the text).
w: p.34: Mountbatten put forth the partition plan, but the Boundary Commission was headed by Radcliff (note 10, p.38).
Chelmsford was the Viceroy under the 1919 Act, not the head of the Boundary Commission.
MacDonald announced the Communal Award of 1932, not the boundaries.

questions.q: On 3 June 1947 the British Government made it clear that a Constitution framed by the Constituent Assembly of India
questions.a: could not apply to parts of the country unwilling to accept it
o: could not apply to parts of the country unwilling to accept it
would apply to all provinces and princely states without exception
would not come into force until approved by the British Parliament
would be drafted by the Viceroy in consultation with the Muslim League
questions.e: p.34: the Constitution could not apply to unwilling parts of the country.
w: This reverses the 3 June 1947 statement: the Constitution could not apply to unwilling parts (p.34).
No British Parliament approval condition is stated for the Constitution (p.34).
The Constituent Assembly framed the Constitution; no drafting role is stated for the Viceroy (p.34).

questions.q: Immediate effect was given to the Mountbatten Plan by
questions.a: the enactment of the Indian Independence Act (1947)
o: the enactment of the Indian Independence Act (1947)
an order of the Viceroy's Executive Council
a resolution of the Constituent Assembly of India
an amendment of the Government of India Act of 1935
questions.e: p.34: immediate effect was given to the plan by enacting the Indian Independence Act (1947).
w: The plan was implemented by an Act, not by an executive order.
The Assembly framed the Constitution; the plan was enacted by Parliament.
A separate Independence Act was enacted; the 1935 Act merely continued as interim law (p.35).

questions.q: Which one of the following correctly describes the reception of the Mountbatten Plan?
questions.a: It was accepted by both the Congress and the Muslim League
o: It was accepted by both the Congress and the Muslim League
It was accepted by the Congress but rejected by the Muslim League
It was accepted by the Muslim League but rejected by the Congress
It was accepted by both parties only after a referendum in every province
questions.e: p.34: the plan was accepted by the Congress and the Muslim League, and given immediate effect by the Independence Act.
w: The Muslim League also accepted it.
The Congress also accepted it.
The text mentions referendums only in the NWFP and Sylhet (p.38 note 10), not in every province.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the passage of the Indian Independence Act, 1947:

1. The boundaries between the two Dominions were determined by a Boundary Commission headed by Lord Mountbatten.
2. The Act abolished the office of Viceroy and provided a Governor-General for each dominion.
3. Each of the two dominions had the right to secede from the British Commonwealth.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: p.38 (note 10): the Boundary Commission was headed by Radcliff; Mountbatten put forth the partition plan. Statement 2 is correct: p.34: the Viceroy's office was abolished; a Governor-General for each dominion. Statement 3 is correct: p.34: the right to secede from the Commonwealth.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.38
'2 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.38
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect: p.38

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the passage of the Indian Independence Act, 1947:

1. The Act dropped the title of Emperor of India from the royal titles of the King of England.
2. The Constituent Assembly of India mentioned in the statement of 3 June 1947 had been formed in 1947.
3. The Act continued British paramountcy over the Indian princely states until each of them acceded.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.35: the title was dropped. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.34: it was formed in 1946. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.35: paramountcy lapsed on 15 August 1947.
w: '2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.35
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.35
'1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.35

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the passage of the Indian Independence Act, 1947:

1. Attlee's announcement was followed by agitation of the Muslim League demanding the partition of the country.
2. The Indian Independence Act came into force on 15 August 1947.
3. Pakistan included the provinces of West Punjab, Sind, Baluchistan, East Bengal and the North-Western Frontier Province, and the district of Sylhet in Assam.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.34: the Muslim League agitated for partition. Statement 2 is correct: p.34 and p.38: in force from 15 August 1947. Statement 3 is correct: p.38: this list of areas.
w: '2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.34
'1 and 2 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.34
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.34

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the passage of the Indian Independence Act, 1947:

1. The princely states were required to obtain the approval of the Secretary of State for Commonwealth Affairs before joining either dominion.
2. The Indian Independence Bill was introduced in the British Parliament on 4 July 1947.
3. Lord Mountbatten became the first Governor-General of the new Dominion of Pakistan.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: p.35: the states were free to join either dominion or remain independent; no such approval is mentioned. Statement 2 is correct: p.38 (note 9): introduced in the British Parliament on 4 July 1947. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.35: Mountbatten became the first Governor-General of the Dominion of India.
w: '3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.35
'1 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.35
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect: p.35

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the passage of the Indian Independence Act, 1947:

1. The princely states were free to join the Dominion of India or the Dominion of Pakistan or to remain independent.
2. The Governor-General of each dominion was to be appointed by the British King on the advice of the dominion cabinet.
3. The Governor-General of India was made a constitutional head, but the provincial governors remained real executive heads acting on their own judgement.
4. The British Monarch was deprived of his right to veto bills, but this right was reserved for the Governor-General.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.35: free to join either dominion or remain independent. Statement 2 is correct: p.34: appointed by the King on the advice of the dominion cabinet. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.35: both the Governor-General and the provincial governors were made constitutional (nominal) heads acting on advice. Statement 4 is correct: p.35: the veto was reserved for the Governor-General.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.35
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.35
'2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.35

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the passage of the Indian Independence Act, 1947:

1. At the stroke of midnight of 14-15 August 1947 British rule ended and power was transferred to the two new independent Dominions of India and Pakistan.
2. The members of the Interim Government of 1946 were members of the Viceroy's Executive Council, with the Viceroy as its head.
3. The partition plan known as the Mountbatten Plan was put forth by the Viceroy, Lord Mountbatten, on 4 July 1947.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.35: power passed to two dominions. Statement 2 is correct: p.36 note: members of the Viceroy's Executive Council; the Viceroy continued as head. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.34: the plan came on 3 June; 4 July is when the Bill was introduced (p.38).
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.35
'2 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.35
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.35

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the passage of the Indian Independence Act, 1947:

1. The Act declared India an independent state from 3 June 1947, the date of the partition plan.
2. The Act proclaimed the lapse of British paramountcy over the Indian princely states from 15 August 1947.
3. The Act empowered the Constituent Assemblies of the two dominions to frame constitutions, but not to repeal Acts of the British Parliament.
4. Immediate effect was given to the Mountbatten Plan by enacting a fresh Government of India Act on the lines of the 1935 Act.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: p.34: independence dated from 15 August 1947; 3 June 1947 is the date of the Mountbatten Plan (p.34). Statement 2 is correct: p.35: paramountcy lapsed from 15 August 1947. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.34: they could repeal any Act of the British Parliament, including the Independence Act itself. Statement 4 is incorrect: p.34: it was the Indian Independence Act, 1947.
w: '4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.34
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.34
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect: p.34

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the passage of the Indian Independence Act, 1947:

1. The referendum in the North-Western Frontier Province and Sylhet was in favour of Pakistan.
2. The members of the Interim Government of 1946 were members of the Council of the Secretary of State for India.
3. The Act abolished the office of Secretary of State for India and transferred his functions to the Secretary of State for Commonwealth Affairs.
4. The Act declared India an independent state from 15 August 1947.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.38 (note 10): both referendums favoured Pakistan. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.36 note: they were members of the Viceroy's Executive Council. Statement 3 is correct: p.35: functions passed to the Secretary of State for Commonwealth Affairs. Statement 4 is correct: p.34: independent from 15 August 1947.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.38
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.38
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.38

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the passage of the Indian Independence Act, 1947:

1. The Act discontinued appointment to civil services by the Secretary of State for India, and the members appointed before 15 August 1947 lost their benefits.
2. The Act continued the office of Viceroy for the Dominion of India, while Pakistan received a Governor-General.
3. The Constituent Assemblies of both dominions were empowered to legislate for their respective territories till the new constitutions were drafted and enforced.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: p.35: earlier appointees continued to enjoy all benefits. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.34: the office of Viceroy was abolished and a Governor-General was provided for each dominion. Statement 3 is correct: pp.34-35: they legislated until the new constitutions were enforced.
w: '2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.35
'1 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.35
'1 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect: p.35

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the passage of the Indian Independence Act, 1947:

1. The Act provided for the partition of India and the creation of two independent dominions, India and Pakistan.
2. The dominions could secede from the British Commonwealth if the British Parliament gave its consent.
3. The Act dropped the title of Emperor of India from the royal titles of the King of England.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.34: two independent dominions. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.34: the right to secede was given to the dominions themselves; no consent is mentioned. Statement 3 is correct: p.35: the title was dropped.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.34
